title: Waiting times: a positive, skewed world
scope: Fictional independent requests under a fixed service configuration. Fit at 20–60 requests/minute; other loads explore extrapolation.
source: Synthetic teaching data: 60 waits generated with seed 918 from a lognormal model. Not measurements of a real service.
assumptions: Analyst interpretation: typical waiting time changes multiplicatively with load, with positive outcomes and a long right tail. This does not establish a queuing mechanism or an intervention effect.
structure: Predictions condition on the supplied inputs; predictor frequencies are not modeled.
Each simulated experiment uses one shared parameter draw and conditionally independent outcomes at the supplied rows.
The lognormal likelihood requires positive outcomes and uses a common residual SD on the log scale. Expected outcomes include the lognormal mean adjustment.

diagnostics: R-hat and divergences are partial computational checks, not evidence of scientific adequacy.

limitations: No external-model refitting, sensitivity reweighting or automatic experiment design.
This snapshot contains a finite scenario grid and posterior draw subset; probabilities have Monte Carlo error.
